mb.photo.design.workstation.storage.note: Nine-track tape and 8-inch floppy disks with magnetic oxide on polymer backing are the standard carriers of the period. Not established: which medium carried the 251137 plot files, at what density, or where handover between design and fabrication occurred.

mb.pcb.laminate.press.release.name: Release paper between books
mb.pcb.laminate.press.release.description: Bleached or unbleached kraft paper laid between each laminate book so resin does not bond one book to the next and the platen stays clean. The same sheet doubles as the cushion that distributes pressure evenly across the book.
mb.pcb.laminate.press.release.note: Kraft paper is lignin-rich cellulose pulp. The paper chain itself is owned by the packaging fragment.

mb.pcb.photoresist.carrier.name: PET carrier film
mb.pcb.photoresist.carrier.description: The polyester backing the resist is laminated from, peeled off after lamination and before exposure, leaving the resist on the copper. It is the same dimensionally stable polyester film as the artwork film stock, and it exists so the 25 um resist can be handled and rolled without touching.
mb.pcb.photoresist.carrier.note: A thin dimensionally stable polyester film carrying the 25 um resist so it can be rolled and handled is ordinary dry-film construction. Not established: the carrier thickness or supplier for the film used on the 250407 board, or the peel timing.

mb.pcb.photoresist.laminate.name: Film lamination of the resist
mb.pcb.photoresist.laminate.description: The board is baked dry, the film is fed from a spool, heated, and pressed onto the copper by rubber-covered nip rollers. The rubber hardness matters: too hard and it embosses the fragile 35 um foil.

facts.label: Control
facts.value: nip rollers and a chill roll to set the film down

mb.pcb.photoresist.laminate.note: Feeding dry film from a spool, heating it and pressing it onto baked-dry copper with nip rollers is ordinary lamination. Not established: the 90-110 deg C window on this line, the roller hardness, or the chill-roll setting used.

mb.pcb.photoresist.coat.name: Surface clean and tack-free prep
mb.pcb.photoresist.coat.description: Before the resist goes on, the board is degreased and dried so the film lies flat. A tack-free prep was unusual on period boards. Wet resist had an easier time of it, which is one reason modern processes moved.
mb.pcb.photoresist.coat.note: Wet resist offered the no-prep advantage. Dry film offered the thickness control. Dry film won on thickness.

mb.solder.wave.preheat.air.name: Recirculating hot-air preheat
mb.solder.wave.preheat.air.description: Preheating is by moving air or radiant tubes, with the zone held below the solder melting point so nothing melts early. Too little preheat gives thermally shocked joints. Too much dries the resin and lifts pads off the laminate. A board full of large electrolytics takes a long time to come through, and preheater capacity is usually what sets the conveyor speed for the whole line.
mb.solder.wave.preheat.air.note: Moving-air or radiant-tube preheat held below the solder melting point is ordinary tunnel practice. Not established: which method the C64 tunnel used, its zone temperatures, or the conveyor-speed limit set by large electrolytics.

mb.pcb.laminate.press.name: Hot platen press and the lamination cycle
mb.pcb.laminate.press.description: The machine that turns loose foil and cloth into a sheet. A hydraulic press pack carries several heated platens so several laminate books can be pressed in one loading, and a stack of foil, prepreg, core and prepreg goes between them. Pressure squeezes out the excess resin and forces it into the weave. The heat completes the cure. The platens are cast and then surface-ground, because a laminate that is not flat is not 1.6 mm everywhere. This one machine is the reason a period FR-4 board has a flatness tolerance tighter than anything the component designer asked for.

facts.label: Press temperature
facts.value: approx. 175 deg C

facts.label: Pressure
facts.value: approx. 1.4 MPa (200 psi)

facts.label: Cycle
facts.value: roughly an hour including cool-down

facts.label: Heat
facts.value: steam coils or embedded electric resistance elements in the platens

mb.pcb.laminate.press.note: Modern high-Tg FR-4 laminates press hotter (200-220 deg C) and harder. Period FR-4 at 175 deg C and 1.4 MPa is the classic cycle.

children.name: Heated platens
children.description: Cast iron platens, machined and surface-ground flat, heated by embedded steam coils or electric resistance elements. The cast iron is chosen for dimensional stability and thermal mass rather than for strength, and the grind is what guarantees that a stack of books comes out of the press uniformly 1.6 mm thick. Grey cast iron is iron ore reduced with coke in a blast furnace.

facts.label: Body
facts.value: grey cast iron, machined and surface-ground

children.note: Not established: that the laminate supplier's press used grey cast iron platens rather than steel, whether heat came from steam coils or embedded electric elements on that press, or the flatness tolerance the surface grind held.

children.name: Hydraulic press pack
children.description: The pressure side of the press: cylinders and platens arranged so that several laminate books are pressed in one loading. The circulating hydraulic oil is a petroleum-derived lubricating fluid, refined from crude alongside almost every other lubricant on the line.
children.note: Pressing several laminate books in one loading with cylinders and platens is the ordinary hydraulic pack. Not established: the cylinder count, operating pressure, or petroleum source of the circulating oil on the laminate supplier press.

children.name: Press heat source
children.description: Steam coils or electric resistance elements in the platens. Gas- or oil-fired central steam was the norm in a laminate plant of this era, which is what makes the press the largest single fuel load on such a site.
children.note: Heating platens with steam coils or embedded electric resistance elements is the ordinary press arrangement. Not established: whether the laminate supplier used gas- or oil-fired central steam or electric heat, or that the press was the largest fuel load on that site.

mb.pcb.laminate.press-cycle.name: Laminate pressing cycle
mb.pcb.laminate.press-cycle.description: One pressing of the laminate book: a stack of foil, prepreg, core and prepreg cured between the heated platens at the period FR-4 cycle (175 deg C and 1.4 MPa), squeezing the excess resin into the weave and completing the cure.
mb.pcb.laminate.press-cycle.note: 175 C and 1.4 MPa are period-typical FR-4 press conditions; the supplier's ramp, soak and cooldown schedule is unrecorded.

mb.pcb.bareboard.fabrication.name: Bare-board fabrication (etch, drill, mask, legend, finish)
mb.pcb.bareboard.fabrication.description: Outside-house sequence of imaging, etching, drilling, masking, legend and finish turning FR-4 laminate into finished bare board fab 250406 ready for insertion.
mb.pcb.bareboard.fabrication.note: Era $1-2 board cost and high etch and drill yield per candidate facts are era quotes, not established as this house cost. Commodore bought laminate and used outside house per laminate node.

mb.pcb.laminate.prepreg.name: B-stage epoxy-glass prepreg
mb.pcb.laminate.prepreg.description: Partly cured B-stage woven E-glass in brominated epoxy, stacked as foil, prepreg, core and prepreg book and press-cured into FR-4.
mb.pcb.laminate.prepreg.note: Resin content 45-60% and gelation 140-160C per laminate facts are period ranges, not established for this supplier prepreg.

mb.pcb.laminate.core.name: FR-4 laminate core
mb.pcb.laminate.core.description: Cured epoxy-glass inner core sheet in the laminate book between prepreg plies, pressed with foil faces into 1.6mm panel.
mb.pcb.laminate.core.note: Core thickness and composition beyond 1.6mm panel with 35um foil per laminate facts are not established.

mb.pcb.legend.colour-ink.name: Coloured epoxy legend ink
mb.pcb.legend.colour-ink.description: Coloured non-white epoxy screen-print ink for extra-colour bands and outlines marking functional regions and PAL or NTSC variant.
mb.pcb.legend.colour-ink.note: Exact colour set on 250407 not confirmed per candidate note; pigment load not established.

mb.pcb.legend.white-ink.name: White epoxy legend ink
mb.pcb.legend.white-ink.description: White epoxy screen-print ink squeegeed through tensioned emulsion-coated mesh and baked onto cured mask for designators and outlines.
mb.pcb.legend.white-ink.note: Mesh count, emulsion type and bake schedule for 250407 legend are not established per candidate note.

mb.pcb.mask.ink.name: Green epoxy solder-mask ink
mb.pcb.mask.ink.description: Green solvent-based epoxy solder-mask ink screen-printed with apertures over pads and holes and thermally or UV cured.
mb.pcb.mask.ink.note: Cure around 150C for half an hour and 0.01-0.02mm thickness per candidate facts are period ranges, not established for this board.
